text.p: Grant Geophysical Inc said Tuesday it has accepted a term sheet for a revised plan of reorganization with Elliott Associates LP of New York.

Under the revised plan, Elliott will purchase substantially all of Grant's assets Grant for a combination of $47.5 million in cash plus the assumption of certain debt, including specifically identified loans totaling $15.1 million.
Previously, Grant President Larry Lenig Jr said, Elliott had agreed to invest a minimum of $30 million with similar debt assumption requirements.
Under the revised plan, secured creditors whose obligations are not assumed will be paid in full in cash.
Unsecured creditors will receive cash from a pool of funds to be established from the investments to be made by Elliott and in connection with the rights offering, Grant said.
Based on the amount of unsecured claims filed, Grant said, it presently estimates cash recovery to allowed unsecured claimholders will be between 50 and 60 percent.
Grant said the revised agreement calls for Elliott Associates to invest $23.75 million directly and to guarantee an additional $23.75 million in new equity capital.

The company said guarantee is in connection with an offering of rights to purchase common stock in the reorganized company. Rights will be issued to the company's unsecured creditors and preferred stockholders.

Grant's common stockholders will not be offered rights in connection with the revised plan, and all currently outstanding and preferred and common stock in Grant will be canceled pursuant to the plan, the company said.
The agreement also calls for a working capital facility of at least $5 million at the time the reorganization plan is consummated.

Grant said the court has set July 7 as the date for submission of the revised plan of reorganization and the accompanying disclosure statement. A hearing on the adequacy of the disclosure statement is scheduled for August 4. Following the hearing, voting on the plan by the Company's creditors and preferred stockholders will take place and a hearing to confirm the plan is scheduled for September 4.

Assuming the plan is confirmed, closing would take within 30 days, the company said. Distributions to creditors will occur immediately following completion of the rights offering but in no event later than December 31.
In connection with the rights proposal, Grant will file a registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission shortly.
In the event that the rights offering has not been completed by December 31, Elliott is obligated to fund the entire additional $23.75 million pending completion of the offering.

Following completion of the rights offering, Elliott will own about 65 percent of Grant and could own up to 100 percent depending on the number of rights exercised by the holders of unsecured debt and preferred stock.
